**Evergreen Park, IL – Seeking Emergency Medicine Core Faculty**
**Join the Physician Partnership Where You Can Increase Your Impact**
Vituity’s ownership model provides autonomy, local control, and a national system of support, so you can focus your attention where you want it to be – on your patients.
  
  
**Join the Vituity Team.**
Vituity is a 100% physician-owned partnership and is led by frontline physicians that are all equitable owners. As an equal and valued partner from day one, our ownership model provides you with financial transparency, a comprehensive benefits package including profit distribution, and multiple career development opportunities. Our leadership understands what your practice needs to thrive and gives you autonomy and local control so you can provide care when, where, and how your patients need it. You are backed by a best-in-class corporate healthcare team and supported by the broad peer-level expertise of 6,000 Vituity clinicians. At Vituity we’ve cultivated an environment where passion thrives, and success comes through shared purpose. We were founded in a culture that values team accomplishments more than individual achievements, an approach we call “culture of brilliance.” Together, we leverage our strengths and experiences to make a positive impact in our local communities. We foster this through shared goals and helping our colleagues succeed, and we also understand the importance of recognition, taking the time to show appreciation and gratitude for a job well done.
  
  
**Vituity Locations:**
Vituity has opportunities at 900 practices across the country, serving 14.5+ million patients a year. With Vituity, if you ever need to move, you can take your job with you.
  
  
**The Opportunity**

* Responsible for teaching/advising residents and fellows.
* Work closely with and support the Residency Program Director – Partner.
* Responsible for following program requirements in accordance with the ACGME and all other accrediting agencies.
* Responsible for supporting and delivering an engaging learning curriculum.
* Ensure that Residency Programs meet all state, federal, and other regulations and guidelines and comply with ACGME standards.
* Oversee and engage with all Residency Core Faculty, Clinical faculty, and Program Coordinators (if applicable).
* Actively participate in recruitment and selection of new residents for admission to the program.
* Assess performance of residents regularly.
* Be a participating member of the Clinical Competency Committee (CCC) and the Program Evaluation Committee (PEC).
* Annually complete the ACGME faculty survey.
* Remain clinically active.
* Mentor and coach residents, advise them regarding their career and educational goals.
* Administer and maintain an educational environment conducive to educating residents in each of the ACGME competency areas.
* Responsible for ensuring safe patient care at all participating sites.
* Responsible for creating an environment of inquiry in the clinical setting.
* Evaluate residents in a timely manner using competency based/milestone evaluations and via direct observation and other relevant evaluation methods.
* Participate in Quality improvement and Patient Safety initiatives.
* Model professional behavior and effectively lead the multidisciplinary team within the system of care delivery.
* Perform an adequate amount of scholarly activity including participation in national organizations and committees and research at the direction of the Residency Program Director – Partner.

**Required Experience And Competencies**

* Physician with current, valid American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) certification or eligibility in relevant field/specialty and an active unrestrictive state license to practice medicine by the state medical board required.
* Licensed physician as a Medical Doctor (M.D.) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (D.O.) required.
* Maintain membership and privileges on Hospital’s medical staff and comply with and abide by the bylaws, rules and regulations, and the policies and procedures of Hospital’s medical staff where services are being provided required.
* Physician Partner status required.
* Experience with leadership/mentorship of residents required.
* Scholarly activity within the last five years preferred.
* Clinical and academic experience to ensure effective implementation of the ACGME program requirements.
* Proficient working knowledge of software applications including Microsoft Word, Excel, Power Point and Outlook.
* Ability to facilitate networking opportunities and create an environment that fosters mentorship and promotes the career advancement of Physician fellows.
* Comprehensive and detailed understanding of national accreditation policies, educational administration, and hospital policies.
* Ability to stay updated with the latest advancements, new developments, research, guidelines, and best practices in the relevant field/specialty.
* Demonstrated proficiency at providing excellent patient care.
* Strong teaching skills to effectively educate and mentor resident physicians.
* Ability to communicate complex medical concepts in a clear and concise manner, use various teaching methods and techniques, and provide constructive feedback to support residents' learning and professional development.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills to effectively interact with residents, colleagues, and other healthcare professionals.
* Active listening skills and the ability to provide clear instructions and feedback and foster a positive learning environment.
* Effective collaboration and teamwork skills.
* Ability to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, ethics, and integrity, including adhering to ethical guidelines, demonstrating a commitment to patient-centered care, maintaining confidentiality, and serving as a professional role model for residents.

**The Practice**
**OSF Little Company of Mary Medical Center – Evergreen Park, Illinois**

* Medium volume (54,000 visits) community ED located on the south side of Chicago.
* Recently remodeled Emergency Department.
* Little Company of Mary if a highly resourced hospital with multiple specialties including labor and delivery.
* Core rotation site for University of Illinois at Chicago EM residents, and most attending shifts are paired up with a UIC EM resident.
* If you are looking for a great practice environment in Chicago with the opportunity for teaching, this is a rare opportunity to find that within the Vituity partnership.

**The Community**

* Evergreen Park, Illinois, is a close-knit south suburb of Chicago that offers small-town warmth with big-city access, making it a great place to live and work.
* Just about 13 miles southwest of downtown Chicago, the village is anchored by Evergreen Plaza, one of the Chicago area's oldest and most iconic shopping centers, alongside a variety of local restaurants and businesses along 95th Street.
* Residents enjoy well-maintained neighborhood parks and recreational facilities perfect for families and outdoor activities.
* Seasonal weather includes snowy winters, blooming springs, warm summers, and colorful autumns, ideal for year-round enjoyment.
* Its location near Midway International Airport and major expressways like I-294 and I-57 make commuting and travel remarkably convenient.
* With strong schools, a tight-knit community feel, and easy access to Chicago's dining, culture, and entertainment, Evergreen Park offers a balanced, welcoming lifestyle for professionals and families alike.

**Benefits & Beyond\***
Vituity cares about the whole you. With our comprehensive compensation and benefits package, we are mindful of what matters most, and support your needs of today and your plans for the future.
  
  

* Superior Health Plan Options
* Dental, Vision, HSA, life and AD&D coverage, and more
* Partnership models allows a K-1 status pay structure, allowing high tax deductions
* Extraordinary 401K Plan with high tax reduction and faster balance growth
* Eligible to receive an Annual Profit Distribution/yearly cash bonus
* EAP and travel assistance included
* Student loan refinancing discounts
* Purpose-driven culture focused on improving the lives of our patients, communities, and employees

We are unified around the common purpose of transforming healthcare to improve lives and we believe everyone has a role to play in that. jobs.title: Tenure-Track or Tenured: Open Rank and Title
jobs.description:
Texas A&M University College of Nursing is seeking two outstanding faculty members with experience in academic nursing education for full-time tenure-track or tenured faculty appointments in Bryan, Texas. These positions carry teaching responsibilities in our nationally ranked undergraduate and graduate programs and are full-time, 9-month appointments with the possibility of a summer contract, beginning August 2026. Applicants will be considered for the titles of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, depending on experience and qualifications. Rank and salary are commensurate with credentials and experience.
  
  
The College of Nursing offers a Bachelor of Science in Nursing with multiple tracks (Traditional, Second Degree, and RN to BSN), a Master of Science in Nursing with concentrations in Family Nurse Practitioner, Nursing Education, and Forensic Nursing, as well as a clinical doctoral program (DNP-Leadership). We also offer a graduate certificate in Forensic Health Care and post-graduate certificates in Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) and Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP). Future plans include launching a PhD program, an LVN to BSN, a BSN to DNP in Forensic Nursing, a DNP in Extreme Environments, and additional graduate and post-graduate certificate programs. We are a growing college within Texas A&M University, with programs located in Bryan, Texas (primary location); Round Rock, Texas; and McAllen, Texas.
  
  
The College of Nursing is one of five health professions colleges within the Health Science Center. Its mission is to educate today’s nurses and tomorrow’s leaders who will transform health and health systems through innovative research and the translation of evidence into practice. The College is committed to addressing health disparities and inequities, with a particular focus on vulnerable and underserved populations. These faculty positions will strengthen the College’s research, teaching, and service portfolio by expanding its established programs in rural health care and advancing nursing practice across various clinical and community settings.
  
  
Texas A&M ranks 13th among US public institutions in total research expenditures ($1.278 B in 2023) and is designated as one of only 71 members of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU), an association of leading public and private research universities in the United States and Canada. Texas A&M is one of only 24 institutions in the nation to hold the triple designation as a land-grant, sea-grant, and space-grant university. As research-intensive positions at a Tier One research university, academic rank is commensurate with prior experience and record. We offer competitive salary, benefits, and startup packages. Consideration will be given to applicants with strong potential for, or an established record of, extramurally funded research programs. Faculty are expected to continue their program of research, seek external funding, and mentor both students and faculty colleagues.
  
  
**Responsibilities Include:**
Tenure-track and tenured faculty members are expected to contribute meaningfully to teaching, research/scholarship, and service within the college and university. Specific responsibilities include:
  
  
Teaching:
  
  
Faculty are expected to teach effectively across classroom, clinical, simulation, and online environments, developing new courses that align with current curricular and accreditation standards. Responsibilities include preparing and revising course materials and assessments to enhance student learning, selecting, and managing high-quality clinical experiences, and providing competent clinical supervision. Faculty also evaluate student performance, advise, and mentor students for academic success, maintain posted office hours, collaborate with and mentor faculty colleagues, and stay current with clinical certifications.
  
  
Research/Scholarship:
  
  
Faculty in tenure-track positions conduct research and scholarship activities in accordance with their rank and appointment expectations. They disseminate findings through publications and presentations, seek competitive external funding to support their research endeavors, and lead or collaborate on scholarly projects that advance nursing education, clinical practice, or health outcomes.
  
  
Service:
  
  
Service involves active participation in college, university, and professional activities, including committee membership, accreditation, or self-study initiatives, advising student organizations, and engaging with the community. Tenured faculty are also expected to mentor junior colleagues and provide leadership within college or university committees and professional organizations or boards.
  
  
The anticipated start date is August 1, 2026.
  
  
**Required Qualifications:**
Earned PhD degree in nursing or in a related field with at least one graduate degree in nursing.
  
  
Clinical expertise in nursing. Candidate must be eligible for a Texas RN and/or APRN license depending upon credentials.
  
  
Demonstrated record of scholarly productivity, extramural funding, or strong potential for obtaining extramural funding. Evidence of research, publication, dissemination, and collaboration must be consistent with expectations for the faculty rank.
  
  
Experience teaching academic nursing (face-to-face, online, or clinical courses) at the baccalaureate or higher level.
  
  
Must be qualified for appointment at the Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor rank, and eligible for tenure consideration at Texas A&M University depending on rank. Tenure determination requires an accomplished record of teaching, research, and service.
  
  
Strong writing, public speaking, and presentation skills.
  
  
Ability to lead and collaborate on interprofessional teams.
  
  
Highly organized and professional demeanor.
  
  
Ability to multi-task and establish effective working relationships.
  
  
Understanding of the mission and role of Land Grant Universities.
  
  
Preferred Qualifications:
  
  
Completion of post-doctoral education.
  
  
Academic degrees granted from more than one degree-granting institution.
  
  
Applicants must apply through the Texas A&M University faculty job board hosted by Interfolio at apply.interfolio.com/174671.
  
  
Applicants should submit the following documents: (1) cover letter (2) detailed curriculum vitae (3) personal statement to include philosophy and plans for research, teaching, and service, as applicable; and (4) contact information for five references.
  
  
For questions regarding the position, contact Jennifer Morton at jmorton@tamu.edu. Academic rank and salary are based on qualifications and experience.
  
  
**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**
Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

jobs.title: Associate Professor/Professor- Nursing
jobs.description:
**Job Description:**
**The Opportunity**
The Department of Nursing in the Manning College of Nursing and Health Sciences (MCNHS) at the University of Massachusetts Boston invites applications for an appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor beginning September 1, 2027.
  
  
This position offers the opportunity to join a diverse community of scholars whose research is advances health equity across local and global settings. We seek an accomplished investigator with an established, externally funded program of research who will sustain and extend that work at UMass Boston, provide scholarly leadership within the Department, and mentor doctoral students and early-career faculty. The successful candidate will benefit from an established culture of collaboration and strong research infrastructure.
  
  
**Our Scholarship**
Nursing scholarship at UMass Boston is grounded in health equity. Our faculty conduct research where health is shaped and delivered, collaborating with communities to address health challenges locally and globally. We welcome applicants whose scholarship aligns with or expands our strengths in areas such as, aging and gerontology, maternal and child health, community-engaged research, and clinically focused science, including cardiovascular health, diabetes, and oncology.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
The successful candidate will:
  
  

* Sustain and expand an externally funded program of research as principal investigator,
* Teach and mentor student, including chairing and serving on dissertation committees
* Mentor early-career faculty in research development, grant proposal preparation, and scholarly productivity
* Provide leadership and service to the Department, College, University, and profession
* Build and sustain research collaborations across the University and with our community partners

**Required**
**What You Will Bring**

* An earned research doctorate (PhD or equivalent) in nursing or a related field
* Eligibility for RN licensure in Massachusetts
* A record of research, teaching, and service that merits appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure at the University of Massachusetts Boston
* Current extramural funding as principal investigator that can be transferred to or sustained at UMass Boston, or a clearly articulated plan to secure such funding upon arrival
* Demonstrated experience mentoring doctoral students, postdoctoral fellows, and/or early-career faculty
* Teaching experience in higher education

Appointment at the rank of Professor additionally requires a national or international reputation in the candidate’s area of science and a sustained history of continuous, competitive extramural funding as principal investigator. Rank and tenure status will be commensurate with the successful candidate’s record and determined through the University’s review process.
  
  
**Preferred**

* An active award that is transferable to UMass Boston
* Experience leading research teams, centers, cores, or training grants
* A record of mentoring colleagues in grant proposal and manuscript development
* Doctoral-level teaching and leadership of dissertation or capstone committees

**What We Offer**
The Manning College and its Office of Research provide internal and external mentoring for faculty, including structured support for grant proposal and manuscript preparation, alongside a wide range of multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary collaborative research opportunities. Faculty appointed at senior rank receive a competitive start-up package, and the College’s pre- and post-award research administration team supports the transfer and ongoing management of existing extramural awards.
  
  
Our faculty collaborate with major academic and medical institutions in and around Boston, including the Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center, UMass Chan Medical School, Boston Children’s Hospital, the Massachusetts Department of Public Health, and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, as well as with community, public, and private health care agencies across the region. The National Cancer Institute funds the University of Massachusetts Boston–Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center partnership; this longstanding collaboration has enabled faculty at both institutions to strengthen and extend partnerships for research on health disparities, PhD training, and community outreach.
  
  
**Our Programs**
The BS, MS, and DNP nursing programs are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE). The MS and DNP programs prepare Family Nurse Practitioners and Adult/Gerontological Nurse Practitioners. The PhD program focuses on health equity, broadly defined.
  
  
Across all programs, our teaching addresses health across the life course among diverse populations, with a sustained focus on improving health equity for populations at risk for health care disparities. For more information, please visit https://www.umb.edu/nursing-health-sciences/
  
  
**Our students**
The University of Massachusetts Boston is the third most diverse university in the country, with more than 60% of our undergraduate students coming from minoritized communities and groups and more than half of our students the first in their families to attend a college or university. Our students come to us from richly diverse life experiences and backgrounds; they bring to our classrooms and research settings the robust range of perspectives growing out of the socio-cultural, economic, and historical contexts in which they have lived, along with the challenges they encounter, engage, and strive to overcome. Faculty are expected to engage and support students with diverse backgrounds and lived experiences through inclusive teaching, advising, and mentoring practices.
  
  
**How To Apply**
To apply, please submit the following: i) cover letter; ii) curriculum vitae (CV); iii) a statement of current and future research plans, including a summary of current and pending extramural support; iv) a statement on teaching philosophy and experience v) a minimum of three professional references, including names and contact information.
  
  
The position will remain open until filled. Questions are welcome at any point in the process. Please contact Dr. Rosemary Samia ( rosemary.samia@umb.edu ), Chair, Nursing Faculty Search Committee.
  
  
UMass Boston expects to pay within an approximate range between $118,500 and $190,000 for this position.
  
  
The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on the consideration of all relevant factors when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.
  
  
UMass Boston is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact HR@umb.edu or 617-287-5150.

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at Virginia Tech seeks applications for multiple tenure track faculty positions at the Assistant or Associate Professor level, depending on experience and qualifications, in the broad area of advanced manufacturing with an anticipated start date of August 2027.
  
  
We seek candidates who will establish an internationally recognized research program in advanced manufacturing. jobs.description:
The Department of Biochemistry and the Center for Plant Science Innovation at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) invite applications for a tenure-track nine-month (academic year) faculty position of open rank (assistant/associate/full professor). This appointment is apportioned as 80% research and 20% teaching. Applicants are sought who will develop a vigorous, internationally recognized research program that seeks to identify novel metabolic pathways, regulatory mechanisms and/or biological processes with the goal of translating findings into strategies for crop improvement and/or bio-based products that support sustainable agriculture and biotechnology to enhance human health. Researchers will be able to leverage UNL’s extensive research infrastructure that includes the Plant Transformation Core Research Facility (PTCRF), multi-location biotech fields, and advanced field and greenhouse phenotyping platforms, to validate and scale their discoveries.
  
  
The Department of Biochemistry provides a robust environment for molecular research, offering access to state-of-the-art resources through shared equipment and the Nebraska Center for Biotechnology. Candidates will have the opportunity to utilize the UNL Cryo-EM facility for structural biology, mass spectrometry for metabolomics and proteomics, and bioinformatics and systems biology computational resources.
  
  
The university offers a highly collaborative environment to develop plant-focused research programs with affiliated resources provided by the University Research Centers (Center for Plant Science Innovation, Center for Integrated Biomolecular Communication, Redox Biology Center, Center for Virology), Holland Computing Center, the Quantitative Life Sciences Initiative, Nebraska Innovation Campus and the Center for Biological Chemistry and Complex Biosystems graduate training programs. The University Research Centers and UNL provide cutting-edge research facilities that support multiple-omics, bioinformatics, supercomputing, flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, TEM, SEM, and metabolic engineering. A competitive start-up package and appropriate laboratory and office space will be offered.

To learn about UNL benefits and your total compensation, please see: **https://go.unl.edu/aboutus**.
  
To learn more about Lincoln, NE at **About Lincoln | Nebraska**.

Minimum Required Qualifications

* Ph.D. or equivalent degree in biochemistry, plant science, or a related field.
* Two or more years of postdoctoral experience.
* Strong record of original research in plant biochemistry as evidenced by peer-reviewed publications.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience in grant writing.
* Experience teaching in biochemistry or related fields.
* Experience with mentoring students.
* Excellent communication skills.
* Expertise in integrated biochemical, structural, and molecular genetic approaches in plant metabolism.
* Demonstrated potential for collaborative research.

  
Posted Salary
  

How to Apply

Click “Apply for this Job” and then “Faculty Application.” Complete the application and attach the following documents:

* A letter of interest that describes your qualifications for the job and anticipated contributions.

* Your curriculum vitae.

* Contact information for three professional references.

* Statements that describe your philosophy and approach to teaching and research.

* A statement describing your experience working in teams or groups and your anticipated contributions to creating environments in which every person and every interaction matters (2 page maximum). See **https://go.unl.edu/ianrguide** for guidance in writing this statement.

Please combine the statements (items 4 and 5) into a single document and attach as “Other Document.”

Position Information

**Be a Tar Heel!**

The Department of English and Comparative Literature in the College of Arts & Sciences at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is looking for an applicant who engages with Critical Game Studies methods and scholarship in their teaching and research. Candidates should utilize interdisciplinary humanities approaches for analyzing, participating, and creating in games studies.
  
  
We welcome approaches that engage in games studies’ major intellectual strands, such as game narratives and narrative critique, game aesthetics, ludology, critical making, design, technology studies, or the rhetoric of games and gaming.
  
  
We seek candidates who are confident in producing cross-disciplinary, collaborative, and experimental games research. A record of research and publication will show the ability to translate hands-on work into theoretically informed and peer-recognized scholarship. Facility with interdisciplinary work will be evident through expertise in multiple areas of study and the creative combination of approaches.
  
  
Our department offers a wide variety of courses in game studies, and we are looking for candidates who are well prepared to teach in our current curriculum, as well as contribute to its ongoing development in this emerging field.
  
  
Candidates will also mentor undergraduate and graduate students in critical game studies and, if relevant, their secondary fields of expertise. Strong evidence of leadership and participation in game studies programs and initiatives will show a collaborative model for academic work. Public outreach, the sharing of resources, and community building will demonstrate generosity and engagement.
  
  
Candidates who apply for this position should demonstrate the traits described above and have a significant investment in critical game studies. They will work regularly with hands-on games studies methods, have a strong record of collaboration and working across disciplinary areas, and read and produce critical game studies scholarship. They may also have expertise in a complementary area of interest that would find a home in a department of English and comparative literature.
  
  
Our department strengths include literary studies; film and media; rhetoric and composition; creative writing; digital humanities; Latina/o studies; and health humanities. We also seek to grow in areas of environmental humanities; disability studies; and new media studies.

  

**Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit**

The Department of English and Comparative Literature is committed to hiring an exceptional teacher/scholar who brings energy and a fresh perspective to their research, pedagogy, and service and who is ready to teach in our Critical Game Studies program. We seek candidates who can contribute to UNC’s academic mission as a public institution, especially through commitment to diversity of perspective, intercultural understanding, and engagement with local resources and communities. We encourage candidates to consult our website to learn about the Department’s curriculum, values, and mission. Candidates working across disciplines are encouraged to apply.
  
  
The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is the flagship institution of a strong state university system comprising 17 campuses across North Carolina; neighbor institutions within 25 miles include Duke University, North Carolina Central University, North Carolina State University, and Meredith College. Chapel Hill is a vibrant college town near the Research Triangle economic hub and 20 minutes from Raleigh-Durham International Airport.

  

**Position Summary**

The Department of English and Comparative Literature at the University of North Carolina at Chapel is recruiting an Assistant Professor of Critical Game Studies. The successful candidate’s duties will include teaching, research, and service. The position will teach a 2-2 load made up of graduate and undergraduate courses; contribute to both undergraduate and graduate curricula; mentor students; participate in select administrative activities; and engage in ongoing scholarly research.

  

**Minimum Education and Experience Requirements**

Ph.D. English or a relevant field and instructional experience at the college level by the time of appointment.

  

**Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience**

Demonstrated excellence in college-level teaching, a strong research portfolio, expertise in research methods, a history of collaboration, experience working in, or with, game studies programs, and evidence of administrative and service experience.

  

**Special Physical/Mental Requirements**

N/A

  

**Campus Security Authority Responsibilities**

Not Applicable.

jobs.description:
The University of Virginia’s Department of Mathematics invites applications for an Assistant Professor (General Faculty) expected to begin August 10, 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates whose career focus is on teaching and learning mathematics and are prepared to contribute to the leadership of our teaching mission in our lower division . The core responsibilities of this position include teaching six courses per year (three each during the spring and fall terms). Additional duties will include serving as a mentor for graduate TAs, providing leadership in our teaching mission, and coordinating the department’s Calculus I & II course offerings. This is a continuing three-year, tenure-ineligible appointment with the possibility but not the guarantee of renewal.

The Department of Mathematics' General Faculty team is a dynamic group that works together to implement evidence-based teaching practices to improve student outcomes in coordinated introductory mathematics courses. Opportunities to participate in graduate TA professional development and/or re-design efforts to improve existing courses may be available.

  

**Minimum qualifications**

By the start of the appointment, applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Mathematics, Mathematics Education, or a related field and have at least 2 years of college-level teaching experience in Mathematics, inclusive of teaching done as a graduate student.

**Preferred qualifications.**

Desirable qualifications include experience coordinating multi-section courses, experience working in a team environment, experience working with students from a wide variety of backgrounds, experience mentoring/developing graduate TAs, and familiarity with the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) in mathematics.

  

To apply, click on Interfolio and submit the following documents:

1. A cover letter describing your skills and experience in the teaching and learning of mathematics and why you are interested in this position. (1-2 pages)

2. A curriculum vitae with the contact information for at least three references.

3. A teaching portfolio. The portfolio should include a statement of your teaching philosophy and provide the committee with a clear picture of your approach to teaching and student learning. Additional materials that illustrate their experience and development as educators are welcome. This might include brief descriptions of curriculum or course design, teaching practices, approaches to assessment, or other examples of effective teaching and learning .

4. Contact information for 3 references.

  

In addition, please submit the following required documents electronically through www.MathJobs.org :

1. A cover letter describing your skills and experience in the teaching and learning of mathematics and why you are interested in this position.

2. An AMS Standard Cover Sheet.

3. A curriculum vitae.

4. A teaching portfolio that will help the committee understand your approach to teaching andlearning. This should contain a personal teaching philosophy. It could include brief descriptions of curriculum design and/or other teaching and learning innovations and practices that reflect who you are.

**Tenure Information:** Tenure Track

The Barney School of Business at the University of Hartford is seeking to fill a tenure-track assistant professor position in business analytics beginning January 2027. Candidates are expected to demonstrate excellence in teaching, scholarly research, and service, and to contribute to the school's mission of preparing students for successful careers in a diverse and data-driven business environment.

The successful candidate will teach courses at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Teaching responsibilities will primarily include business analytics courses such as statistical methods, data mining and big data, database management, data visualization, artificial intelligence, and programming for business applications. The candidate should also be prepared to teach general business courses as needed and may have the opportunity to teach general education and interdisciplinary courses. Many graduate courses are delivered in online, face-to-face, and hybrid formats, and faculty are expected to teach effectively across modalities while incorporating current technologies and innovative pedagogical approaches.

**Description**:

The Department of Physics at the University of Houston invites applications for a tenure-track position at the level of Assistant Professor for a theoretical physicist in quantum information theory and many-body systems, to begin in Fall 2027. This position is part of the university-wide Presidential Frontier Faculty (PFF) initiative and seeks candidates whose research advances the theoretical foundations of quantum science.
  
  
We are particularly interested in candidates whose work bridges quantum information theory, quantum algorithms, and entanglement structure to quantum many-body physics, electronic structure theory, or complex emergent phenomena. Applicants should have a strong track record of research and demonstrate the potential to develop a vigorous, externally funded research program. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to our growing efforts in quantum materials, condensed matter theory, and computational physics, while fostering collaborations across departments, including mechanical engineering, computer science, and mathematics.
  
  
The new faculty member will teach both undergraduate and graduate courses and mentor students and postdoctoral researchers in a robust academic environment. A Ph.D. in Physics or a closely related field is required. Postdoctoral experience in theoretical quantum science, quantum information, or AI-enhanced physics is strongly preferred. Competitive candidates will demonstrate strong communication skills and show promise in securing federal funding (e.g., NSF, DOE) and contributing to multi-investigator, interdisciplinary initiatives.
  
  
This position aligns with national and state-level priorities in Quantum Information Science. It is supported by a vibrant research environment at the University of Houston, a Carnegie Tier One public research institution. The new hire will have access to a strong network of collaborators across campus and be well positioned to participate in center-level research proposals and initiatives.
  
  
Application Instructions: Applicants should submit a cover letter, a teaching statement, a statement of research interests and plans (including strategies for involving students and seeking external support), a full curriculum vitae with a list of publications, and contact information for at least three professional references.
  
  
All materials must be submitted online at:
  
https://uh.edu/provost/faculty/faculty-resources/prospective-faculty/
  
  
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. For full consideration, applications should be received by December 1, 2026. Inquiries may be directed to Prof. Pavan Hosur at phosur@central.uh.edu.

Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of Texas for the duration of their appointments.
  
  
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
  
  
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e., communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems, electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the security and integrity of the research is maintained.
  
  
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor, Communication Studies
jobs.description:
**Job Description Summary**

The Department of English and Media Studies at Bentley University invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position in communication studies, to begin July 1, 2027. We are interested in candidates whose research incorporates humanistic, qualitative, and/or design research methodologies.

The successful candidate will be able to teach existing courses such as Multimodal Communication, Introduction to Communication Studies, Introduction to Mass Communication, Intercultural Communication, and/or Public Speaking for Professional Success (at the undergraduate and/or graduate-level), as well as develop new courses to meet the needs of contemporary undergraduates.

Tenure-track faculty teach a 2-2 load for their first three years and a 3-2 load for their final two years before applying for tenure. Standard teaching load for tenured faculty is 3-2, with the potential for additional course releases for exceptional creative/scholarly production.

Bentley is committed to the teacher-scholar model where teaching, scholarship, service and community engagement are expected and valued. We seek qualified faculty who represent diverse backgrounds, interests, and talents and share a commitment to high ethical standards and a willingness to embrace challenge and change.

The English and Media Studies Department offers an array of courses in literature, film, communication, creative writing, and media production. We actively engage students through several innovative degree paths to complement students pursuing business-related professions, including majors in English, Creative Industries, and Film and Media and minors in Gender and Sexuality, Media Management, and Ethnic Studies. Serving as the hub for writing and media, the department also houses the Climate Creativity Lab, Writing Center, ESOL Center, and Film and Media Studies Lab.

Bentley University, located in suburban Boston, is an AACSB and NECHE accredited institution that enrolls approximately 5,500 students at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels. Bentley is ranked at or near the top in several categories by US News & World Report, including Best Regional Universities North and Most Innovative Schools, with Bloomberg ranking Bentley in the top 20 undergraduate business programs. Bentley’s high graduation and retention rates and top-ranked Pulsifer Career Center reflects a commitment to student success and inclusiveness. With a strong faculty of teacher-scholars, Bentley strives to be a “Force for Good” through the integration of business with the arts and sciences, and a strong emphasis on ethics and social responsibility. Providing a stimulating academic community for faculty, staff, and students, Bentley supports its faculty as they pursue cutting-edge research and bring their expertise and real world understanding into the classroom.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

PhD in Communication or related field, or other terminal degree. ABD candidates will be considered. The successful hire will need to have terminal degree in hand by September 1, 2027.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

Candidates should have experience as the instructor of record for an introductory course in communication (e.g., public speaking or an introductory/gateway course in communication, media studies, or design). Candidates should also have one or more peer-reviewed scholarly publications or juried works.

  

**Application Instructions:**

For full consideration, candidates must submit the following as part of the application before November 1, 2026:

  

* An up-to-date curriculum vitae
* Cover letter
* A writing sample or creative/design equivalent
* A Teaching Statement, which should include a description of how the faculty member has demonstrated or intends to create and support an inclusive classroom environment
* A research statement
* A sample syllabus for a 200- or 300-level elective course

We request all materials to expedite search processes. To expedite the search and increase equity, all semifinalist and finalist interviews will be held virtually.

**Pay Transparency:**

At Bentley we offer a “total rewards” package designed to attract, motivate, retain, and reward our employees. This includes competitive compensation, robust benefits, career development and opportunities, generous paid time off, workplace flexibility and a positive, engaging employee experience. In alignment with the Massachusetts Pay Transparency Act and our commitment to equity and transparency, we’re sharing the salary grade range for this role. The grade range is based on market data and the scope of responsibilities. Final pay will depend on your experience, education, and other relevant qualifications.

**Salary Ranges (depending on rank, qualifications and experience):**

* Assistant Professor: $72,738 - $88,901

If you have questions about the salary grade range or need additional information, please contact us at GA\_HR\_Employment@bentley.edu.

Bentley University requires references checks and may conduct other pre-employment screening.

**DIVERSITY STATEMENT**

Bentley University strives to create a campus community that welcomes the exchange of ideas, and fosters a culture that values differences and views them as a strength in our community.

Bentley University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, building strength through diversity. The University is committed to building a community of talented students, faculty and staff who reflect the diversity of global business. We strongly encourage applications from persons from underrepresented groups, individuals with disabilities, covered veterans and those with diverse experiences and backgrounds.

Position Information

**Be a Tar Heel!**

The Department of Music at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a Teaching Assistant Professor of Music with expertise in Opera and Voice. We seek a pedagogically innovative and collaborative colleague who will direct UNC Opera and teach studio voice within the context of a broad liberal arts curriculum. This position is particularly well suited to a singer-teacher and opera director who is passionate about working with singers in a performance program that is undergraduate-only and welcomes students with a wide range of musical backgrounds, interests, and levels of prior experience. UNC Opera typically performs a scenes program in the fall and a full production in the spring. This course emphasizes the musical and dramatic aspects of role preparation and staging, rather than high-concept productions. Candidates with experience teaching across musical genres and styles, including classical, musical theatre, and contemporary vocal repertoire, are especially encouraged to apply.

  

**Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit**

The Department of Music at UNC-Chapel Hill offers a BMus and BA in Music for undergraduate students and an MA and Ph.D. in Musicology for graduate students. Our educational mission is to teach music majors and non-majors, to connect the study of music to a broader understanding of the world, and to guide graduate students as researchers and teachers. We serve the public by presenting performances and academic lectures by students, faculty, and guest artists and scholars. We offer over one hundred concerts and recitals each year, and our facilities include a state-of-the-art auditorium with recording capabilities (audio and video) as well as lighting and sound systems. Our 60 full-time and part-time faculty teach approximately 2500 students during the academic year and another 200 during summer school. jobs.description:
**Position Summary**
--------------------

**Job Description:**
  
The Department of Visual and Performing Arts at York College of Pennsylvania invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Graphic Design in the Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) degree program beginning in August 2027. We seek an engaged educator and active practitioner with dedicated expertise in User Experience/User Interface Design and Motion Graphics. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in advancing our curriculum in interactive media, delivering high-impact studio instruction, and contributing to the academic and professional development of our undergraduate students.
  
York College of Pennsylvania (YCP) thrives on cross-disciplinary collaboration, active creative practices, and faculty mentorship. We are a tight-knit community where your voice shapes the curriculum, your active studio practice is celebrated, and our gallery system and industry-standard studios provide a vibrant canvas for both you and YCP students. Located near major creative and cultural centers throughout the Mid-Atlantic region (Baltimore, New York City, Philadelphia, and Washington, D.C.), we are situated in a region with thriving creative entrepreneurship opportunities and community-engaged art. YCP can offer the perfect launchpad to connect your students with major cultural hubs while thriving in a supportive, collaborative peer environment. Additionally, the York art community provides opportunities for professional networking, internships, industry partnerships, and community engagement. York City's vibrant arts community further supports creative entrepreneurship, experiential learning, and partnerships that connect students with contemporary design practice.
  
  
**Outcome:**
  
The successful candidate will teach an engaging mix of foundational and advanced BFA courses, spanning from typography, identity systems, design research, and professional practice to UX/UI, and motion graphics with the opportunity to modernize and expand program offerings to reflect emerging trends in interactive media, emerging technologies, and contemporary design practice. Beyond cultivating student excellence in the studio environment, the successful candidate will provide dedicated mentorship through academic advising, engage in service to our academic community, and maintain a robust, active creative or scholarly practice supported by the institution.

**Essential Functions**
-----------------------

* Teach four 3-credit courses per semester (Fall and Spring)
* Provide mentorship to students via academic advising
* Service to the college community
* Maintain an active scholarly and/or creative practice

**Experience and Education Required**
-------------------------------------

We are looking for a collaborative colleague who can bring a healthy mixture of classroom experience and real-world insight.
  
**Required:**

* Terminal degree in Graphic Design, Interactive Media, Visual Communication, or a closely related field (MFA or equivalent).
* Demonstrated expertise in UX/UI Design and Motion Graphics software/workflows.
* Evidence of an active, high-level professional practice or scholarly record.
* A clear commitment to undergraduate teaching excellence and student mentorship with a minimum of two years of college-level teaching practice.

**Preferred:**
  

* Minimum of three years of professional experience in the graphic design industry.
* Experience with cross-disciplinary collaboration or community-partnered design projects.
* Knowledge of emerging design technologies, including evolving AI-assisted workflows, accessibility standards, and creative entrepreneurship.

**Required Skills and Qualifications**
--------------------------------------

Additional Required Skills and Qualifications:

* Excellent communication skills and commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration.
* Ability to supervise and motivate undergraduate students.

  
To ensure full consideration, please submit the following materials electronically:
  
  
1. Cover letter detailing your teaching philosophy and professional practice
  
2. Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  
3. Link to digital portfolio of professional work
  
4. Link to portfolio of student work from courses taught
  
5. Unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts
  
6. Contact information for three confidential letters of recommendation

York College of Pennsylvania is an Equal Opportunity Employer and Non-Discriminatory. For a copy of York College's Annual Security Report, you may contact the Office of Campus Safety or visit the website: Annual Security Report.

jobs.title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor, Digital Humanities
jobs.description:
**Job Description Summary**

The Department of English and Media Studies at Bentley University invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor, to begin July 1, 2027. We seek candidates with a record of creative scholarship and innovative teaching in the fields of Digital Humanities and/or New Media Studies. We particularly welcome applications from scholars whose research and teaching will broaden our curriculum and support the diverse needs of our undergraduate students.

The candidate appointed to this position will be prepared to teach an introductory course in Digital Humanities and/or New Media and to develop new courses in their area of expertise. In addition, the successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to teach existing courses, including Critical Reading and Writing and/or Multimodal Communication.

Tenure-track faculty teach a 2-2 load during their first three years and a 3-2 load during their final two years before applying for tenure. The standard teaching load for tenured faculty is 3-2, with the potential for additional course releases for exceptional creative and scholarly production. Candidates are also expected to maintain a strong teaching portfolio and contribute through departmental and university service.

Bentley is committed to the teacher-scholar model where teaching, scholarship, service and community engagement are expected and valued. We seek qualified faculty who represent diverse backgrounds, interests, and talents and share a commitment to high ethical standards and a willingness to embrace challenge and change.

The English and Media Studies Department offers an array of courses in literature, film, communication, creative writing, and media production. We actively engage students through several innovative degree paths to complement students pursuing business-related professions, including majors in English, Creative Industries, and Film and Media and minors in Gender and Sexuality, Media Management, and Ethnic Studies. jobs.title: Assistant Professor (TT)- Electrical & Computer Engineering- Power Electronics Devices & Systems
jobs.description:
* 509974

* Amherst, Massachusetts, United States

* Academic Year (9 Months)
* Full Time
* MSP
* On Site
* Riccio College of Engineering

* Faculty

* Opening on: Oct 1 2026

**Executive Area:** Academic Affairs

**College/School/MBU:** Engineering

**Department:** Elect & Computer Engineering

**Work Location:** Amherst

**Schedule:** Full Time

**Work Arrangement:** Onsite

**Job Summary**

The Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering (ECE) at the University of Massachusetts Amherst is seeking talented applicants for a tenure-track assistant professor position in Power Electronics. Under exceptional circumstances, highly qualified candidates at other ranks may receive consideration. The appointment is expected to begin September 1, 2027.
  
  
We will strengthen our commitment to recruiting and retaining diverse and exceptional global talent by advancing a community of success, wellness, and inclusivity. As the flagship public land-grant university of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, we expand educational access, fuel innovation and creativity, and share and use our knowledge for the betterment of the world. We embrace our responsibility to advance the inclusive and equitable well-being of all people and the health of our planet.
  
  
The position is defined broadly across the full scope of power electronics and power conversion engineering. Scholars working across disciplines or in nontraditional or emerging areas of power electronics are particularly encouraged to apply. Demonstrated connections or potential for partnership with industry and national laboratories is a plus.
  
  
Specific areas of interest include but are not limited to:
  
  
Wide bandgap (WBG) semiconductor and oxide devices and their application in power conversion systems
  
  
Design, control, and optimization of power electronic converters and inverters
  
  
Grid-connected power electronics, motor drives, microgrids, and distributed energy resources
  
  
This position is part of the department's strategic growth in energy systems and electrification, aligned with the university's Energy Transition Institute and the new Sustainable Engineering Laboratories building. We are committed to expanding the scope of our department beyond our traditional strengths.
  
  
As a campus, college, and department with an increasingly diverse student body, we are looking for candidates who can operate effectively in a diverse faculty and student community, and who value collegiality, collaboration, achievement, and integrity. We encourage applications from individuals with a commitment to mentor under-represented demographics within engineering. We welcome candidates who have had non-traditional career paths, those who have paused their careers for family or other reasons, or who spent time outside of academia.

**Essential Functions**

The candidate is expected to develop an externally-funded research program in power electronics engineering and develop and maintain an internationally recognized scholarly presence. External funding sources in this area include NSF (ECCS, CBET, ERC programs), DOE (EERE, ARPA-E), DARPA, and industry partnerships.
  
  
The candidate is expected to contribute to teaching existing graduate and undergraduate courses in related areas, and will be encouraged to develop creative new curricula in areas of their expertise, including courses supporting the department's power and energy systems academic program.
  
  
The candidate is also expected to contribute meaningful service to their department, College, University, and externally within their field through participation in committees, faculty governance, and activities that support the academic community.

**Other Functions**

Other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications**

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a closely related field, or anticipate having such a degree by August 31, 2027.

**Additional Details**

The ECE Department is an inclusive and vibrant academic community, with 45 full-time faculty members, approximately 270 graduate students, and 775 undergraduates. Research expenditures exceeded $13.4M in the most recent fiscal year. The department has broad research strengths and is actively growing its presence in power electronics and energy systems. Additional information about the department can be obtained at umass.edu/engineering/ece.
  
  
The Daniel J. Riccio Jr. College of Engineering is recognized as one of the top 35 public engineering schools in the nation by *U.S. News & World Report* and is the #1 public engineering program in New England. Our inclusive and dynamic community includes approximately 2,700 undergraduate and 650 graduate students, and 160 instructional faculty across five engineering departments. With over $69 million in research expenditures and 20+ affiliated research centers and programs, we're at the forefront of discovery. For more on the Riccio College of Engineering, visit: https://www.umass.edu/engineering/.
  
  
Our new Sustainable Engineering Laboratories building offers immersive labs and learning spaces, enabling us to test and develop technologies that address real-world sustainability challenges — a natural home for cutting-edge power electronics research. The College strives to be a leader in transformative engineering education, supporting faculty through various initiatives including our membership in the Kern Entrepreneurial Engineering Network (KEEN).
  
  
UMass Amherst is a leader in providing institutional support for faculty to combine work and family/personal responsibilities, and has been listed among the Chronicle of Higher Education's "Great Colleges to Work For." UMass maintains a nationally recognized ADVANCE Institutional Transformation program that seeks to increase equity in STEM fields (https://www.umass.edu/advance/). For more information on work-life balance at UMass Amherst, see https://www.umass.edu/faculty-development/prospective-faculty/work-here/work-life-balance.
  
  
This position is subject to final budgetary and administrative approval.

**Working Conditions**

Work is performed in a standard office or indoor university environment and involves minimal physical exertion.

**Work Schedule and Work Arrangement**

Full-time, academic year position. Schedule varies depending on teaching, research, and service.

**Salary Information**

The University expects to pay within an approximate range between $79,350 and $137,344 for this position.
  
  
The low end of the pay range in all faculty searches at the University of Massachusetts Amherst is the minimum salary for the rank included in the collective bargaining agreement between the University and the Massachusetts Society of Professors, UMass Amherst/MTA/NEA. Engineering tenure-track starting salaries are typically well above this minimum.
  
  
The high end of the pay range reflects the 75th percentile for the department/discipline based on established, disciplinary-specific faculty compensation surveys.
  
  
The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on consideration of all relevant factors, including faculty rank and required or relevant certifications, when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.

**Special Instructions for Applicants**

Candidates must provide the following materials in their application package, addressed to the "Power Electronics Search Committee." Applications will be reviewed starting on January 1, 2027 and will be reviewed until the search is completed. Applications submitted by the priority deadline will receive full consideration. All files must be provided in .pdf format. **Applicants must disclose whether and to what extent AI tools were used in the preparation of their application package.**
  
  
Cover letter **(1 page)** — addressed to the "Power Electronics Search Committee." The letter should a) introduce yourself, b) briefly describe your research interests and alignment with this position, and c) describe your interest in and alignment with the mission and vision of the Riccio College of Engineering.
  
  
Overall vision statement **(2 pages)** — Candidates should describe the overall vision of what they would like to accomplish in their career, integrating across all aspects of teaching, research, outreach, and service, and discuss the inspiration that will sustain them in this faculty position.
  
  
Research statement **(2 pages)** — Candidates should situate their past research in a broader scholarly context and give their research vision for this position. Candidates are specifically asked to mention the types of scholarship they will perform, how that scholarship will be disseminated, expectations for how that scholarship will be funded, collaboration potential, and any connections to community engagement, broadening participation in STEM, or grand challenges in engineering. Statements will be evaluated based on demonstrated excellence or demonstrated promise of future excellence.
  
  
Teaching and mentoring statement **(2 pages)** — Candidates should address teaching and mentoring of graduate and undergraduate students, as well as recruiting of graduate students. Candidates should describe their past teaching and mentoring experience and express their vision for educating the next generation of engineers. Candidates are specifically asked to mention existing courses in power electronics and energy systems they are qualified to offer, and courses they are interested in developing. Please discuss any plans for making engineering engaging to all students.
  
  
Curriculum vitae — Typically ordered as follows: 1) education, 2) employment, 3) awards and honors, 4) sponsored research (if any), 5) peer-reviewed publications, 6) service, and 7) other sections as appropriate.
  
  
Professional references — Contact information (name, title, email address, institution) for three professional references. At least one reference must be from a current or former supervisor. References will not be contacted until the second phase of the search.
  
  
**Process**
  
  
The steps of the search process are as follows:
  
  
A minimally qualified pool is identified from the applicants, ideally by mid-January 2027.
  
  
All remaining candidates are evaluated and a long list of approximately 10–15 candidates is identified; these candidates will be invited to preliminary interviews via video conference. Candidates invited to these interviews will be notified at least one week before the scheduled date.
  
  
Reference letters will be requested from candidates advancing to the short list stage.
  
  
A short list of approximately 5 candidates is developed from the long list; these candidates will be invited to interview on campus. We anticipate on-campus interviews in February–March 2027, completing before spring break.  
  
  
  
*This position will remain open for the time period required by any applicable collective bargaining agreement and will continue until a suitable candidate pool is identified. Interested applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early.*

The Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame in Notre Dame, Indiana, invites applications for an endowed Chair professorship, appointed at the rank of full professor, in Catholic systematic theology. **Faculty Position – Osteopathic Principles & Practices / NMM/OMM**
The Meritus School of Osteopathic Medicine (MSOM), located on the campus of Meritus Health in Hagerstown, Maryland, is actively expanding its faculty. As the first new medical school in Maryland in more than a century, MSOM is committed to advancing osteopathic medical education, strengthening the physician workforce, and improving the health of the region through excellence in teaching, scholarship, and service.

**faculty appointment in Osteopathic Principles & Practices (OPP) / Neuromusculoskeletal Medicine (NMM/OMM)**

jobs.title: History of Architecture and the Designed Environment Faculty Position in Design Justice
jobs.description:
Required Qualifications:

* PhD in Architecture, Architectural History, History of Art, or a closely related field by the start date of the appointment.
* 1 academic year of experience teaching at the collegiate, graduate, and/or professional level (this may include part time graduate teaching experience).
* A demonstrated interest in intersecting teaching, scholarship, and/or service with design justice.
* Potential to develop a strong record of achievement in scholarship.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Demonstrated experience in securing grant funding to support research related to the history of architecture and the designed environment.
* Commitment to collaborative and interdisciplinary approaches to research and teaching.

The University of Minnesota’s College of Design invites applications for a tenure-track position in the Department of Architecture, Landscape Architecture, and Interior Design (ALI), with a focus on the history of architecture and the designed environment. We are seeking tenure-track candidates who are committed to advancing a scholarly, pedagogic, and/or service agenda specifically focused on design justice either through the history of architecture and the designed environment teaching, and/or in research, practice, or service to the disciplines of architecture, landscape architecture or interior design. This is a 100%-time academic year (9-month) position at the level of assistant professor. Salary range: $80,000 - $85,000.

We seek applicants whose work focuses on architecture and design from the mid-twentieth century onward. Preference will be given to those whose interests, especially in teaching, engage with each of the ALI disciplines. The successful candidate will also have a strong commitment to design justice, and eventually, the opportunity to participate in the College of Design’s Design Justice Collective.

Responsibilities

* Teach undergraduate and graduate architectural history courses, some of which will integrate landscape architecture, interior design history, and design justice. Teaching should contribute to students’ understanding of and design for the contexts in which they will practice; and emphasize critical perspectives and intersections among cultural and global contexts.
* Conduct research on the history of architecture, the designed environment, and design justice. Develop a strong record of publication and dissemination.
* Provide service to the Department (including serving on the Design Justice Collective), the University, and the community typical of tenure-track faculty.
* Advise/mentor undergraduate and graduate students, and contribute to recruitment and retention strategies for students who have been historically underinvested.

Situated within the College of Design, the Department of Architecture, Landscape Architecture, and Interior Design (ALI) was established in 2023 to enhance interdisciplinary connections between programs that until recently were in different departments, and in the case of Interior Design, on a different campus. ALI’s studios, classrooms, workshop, and library are located in Rapson Hall. The building was designed by Thorshov & Cerny in 1960, renovated with an addition by Steven Holl in 2002, and named for the former head of the School of Architecture, architect Ralph Rapson.

ALI is committed to a diverse, socially engaged, contextually sensitive, ecologically responsible, and technologically rich vision of design. Its students, faculty, and programs are known for their history of design excellence, and their strong relationships with an exceptional practice community. They are well positioned to work together with culturally diverse local communities committed to race and climate justice, through a curriculum that actively pursues engaged design, research, and scholarship in the College, University, and beyond.

ALI enrolls over 800 students, including more than 450 undergraduates in architecture (Pre-Architecture, BDA, and BS in Architecture), approximately 100 graduate students in the NAAB accredited Master of Architecture degree, about 70 students in the professionally accredited BLA and MLA programs, and 150 in the professionally accredited BS in Interior Design program.  
The department’s faculty includes internationally recognized experts in a range of interrelated architectural fields: design; urban and rural design; building technology; digital design and representation, design/build; ecological design and sustainable building design; resilient and regenerative infrastructures; housing; heritage studies and public histories; critical practice and representation; history, theory, and criticism; and research embedded in practice.

About the College of Design

The University of Minnesota Twin Cities is located on traditional, ancestral, and contemporary lands of the Dakota People, ceded in the Treaties of 1837 and 1851. We are committed to recognizing the complex history of this land by honoring the truth of violence, displacement, migration, and settlement that bring us together now. We acknowledge the need to end the violence against missing and murdered Indigenous women– a local and national epidemic which can be traced back to the arrival of European colonizers across Turtle Island. We acknowledge and fight against the legacy of white supremacy and culture of anti-Black racism in our own community, which has led to the murders of Jamar Clark, Philando Castile, George Floyd, Daunte Wright, Winston Smith, and countless other Black Americans across this nation. Black lives matter. We stand with our Hmong, Asian, Asian-American, and Pacific Islander communities against the rise of xenophobic violence since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic. We recognize that words are not enough and we remain committed to the work of eradicating the injustices against all Black, Indigenous, and people of color caused by systemic racism.

Formed in 2006, the University of Minnesota’s College of Design encompasses a full range of design disciplines, including apparel design, graphic design, product design, human factors and ergonomics, retail and consumer studies, and heritage studies and public history, in addition to architecture, landscape architecture, and interior design. We offer eight undergraduate degrees, twenty-four graduate and professional degree options, and nine centers for research, creative scholarship, and engagement. Through rigorous commitments to creativity, equity, and advancing technologies, College of Design educational programs and innovations address emerging issues, identify problems, frame creative approaches, and generate solutions across all scales of human experience. We offer rich opportunities for interdisciplinary research and public engagement, through highly-regarded research and engagement centers, including the Center for Retail Design and Innovation (CRDI), Wearable Product Design,Digital Design Center (DDC), Minnesota Design Center (MDC), Center for Sustainable Building Research (CSBR), and the Goldstein Museum of Design. For more information about the college, please visit our website at design.umn.edu.

We are located in the Twin Cities, known as a major design hub and home to design-oriented Fortune 500 companies such as Target, 3M, General Mills, Best Buy, and Medtronic, several international and national award-winning architecture practices, thriving local businesses, and a strong non-profit sector. Our students have a wide range of internship opportunities, our graduates enjoy high employment rates, and our alumni are highly engaged with current students and faculty. We take pride in Minnesota’s designations as a Research 1 and Community-Engaged University, which provide foundations for many of our award-winning projects.

The University of Minnesota, a Class 1 research institution, enables connections with faculty and students in a broad range of disciplines. The Institute for Advanced Study supports interdisciplinary collaboratives and programs. The Northwest Architectural Archives holds an extensive collection of architectural drawings and related ephemera, and the University of Minnesota Press is known for its architecture publications. For more information, see: https://twin-cities.umn.edu/about-us.

Applications must be submitted online. To be considered for this position, please click the Apply button and follow the instructions. You will be given the opportunity to complete an online application for the position and attach a cover letter and resume. To be fully considered for this position, please submit the following:

* A cover letter outlining your teaching approach, research interests, and how you would contribute to the Design Justice Collective.
* Curriculum vitae.

**Description**:

The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering in the Cullen College of Engineering at the University of Houston invites applications for a full-time, non-tenure-track, position at the rank of Instructional Assistant Professor or Instructional Associate Professor, beginning Fall 2027.
  
  
The successful candidate will contribute to the department’s expanding aerospace and space systems programs through teaching, curriculum development, and student mentoring. Teaching responsibilities could include undergraduate and graduate courses in areas such as Aerospace Design, Dynamics and Control of Space Vehicles, Space Propulsion, Orbital Mechanics, and Aerospace Systems Laboratory. Assignments will reflect the candidate’s expertise and departmental needs and may include foundational mechanical engineering courses.
  
  
Responsibilities could also include developing hands-on design and laboratory experiences, supervising capstone projects, mentoring multidisciplinary student teams, student advising, assessment of student learning, continuous program improvement, and departmental service. The position offers an opportunity to help shape the department’s undergraduate aerospace curriculum and future program initiatives.

Its aerospace education and research activities include the NASA-funded IDEAS² Center and the Sasakawa International Center for Space Architecture (SICSA). The University of Houston is a public, Carnegie-designated R1 research university located in Houston, a global hub for aerospace, energy, and biomedical innovation.

Candidates must demonstrate a strong commitment to engineering education, evidence of effective teaching or clear potential for teaching excellence, and excellent written and oral communication skills in English.
  
  
Experience in aerospace design instruction, capstone supervision, laboratory development, or multidisciplinary project-based learning is highly desirable. Relevant aerospace industry or government laboratory experience, as well as experience developing industry-sponsored projects or engaging aerospace professionals in student learning, is also desirable.

jobs.description:

The Assistant Professor of Mathematics Education will promote our Catholic Franciscan mission and Identity by teaching mathematics methods and content courses in Marian’s elementary education program and will also be responsible for coordinating and supervising teacher candidates in their field placements.

In addition to teaching, candidates are expected to engage in research and in service to the department, college, university, and profession. Teaching-focused candidates with experience or expertise in K-8 mathematical preparation are encouraged to apply. The successful applicant would serve in a dual-appointment role with the Fred S. Klipsch Educators College and the Department of Mathematical & Computational Sciences.

The Fred S. Klipsch Educators College is recognized as an A+-rated elementary mathematics education program. The mission of the Educators college is to attract, prepare, develop, and support teachers and leaders who are guided by Franciscan values, informed by theory, and exemplary in practice. The Department of Mathematical & Computational Sciences is a collaborative academic community committed to fostering student engagement, problem solving, and communication. The department offers degrees in both Mathematics and Computer Science to develop transformative leaders for service to the world in a variety of areas of business, government and education.
